top_story: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon killed 11 people on 15 August, including three children, shattering the relative calm of the June truce and sharply raising the risk that the Lebanon front will again overtake Gaza as the most volatile arena on Israel’s borders. That escalation lands amid a sustained human toll already visible in Beirut hospitals, where children wounded in earlier Israeli attacks are facing life-altering injuries that underscore how cross-border violence is reverberating far beyond frontline villages. In Gaza, a 13 August strike that killed two people showed the lower-intensity but continuing pattern of Israeli operations, even as the regional military picture is shaped by US attrition in the Iran war, including the loss of roughly a quarter of its Reaper drones and pressure on munitions stocks. The combined effect is a more brittle regional environment in which Israeli force escalation, strained US military capacity, and mounting civilian harm are reinforcing each other rather than containing the conflict.
